Next: anti-churn fixes (user-approved). In the last Sonnet replay JNJ was bought and sold 8 times and OKE, MO, PEP, WMT, COP and LOW also flipped; the full-exit-only cooldown didn't catch partial trims and top-ups.
1. Make portfolio rebalancing weekly (a configurable day) by default. Daily runs still do monitoring and alerts, and may only trade on hard triggers: a risk-limit breach, stop or drawdown rules, a material cited event (8-K, earnings, guidance) that changes the thesis, or a new high-conviction entry above a threshold.
2. Cooldown of N sessions (default 10) after ANY trade on a name, in either direction, unless a hard trigger fires.
3. Thesis-change gate: a trade on an existing holding must cite what changed since the last decision on that name (new fact_refs dated after it). Otherwise it's blocked and logged.
4. A minimum trade size (dollars and % of book) so tiny $1 trims don't happen; the no-trade band applies to drift.
5. Add a turnover and round-trip metric to the replay report, plus a test that recreates the JNJ flip pattern and asserts it's blocked.
Also, EIA is skipped permanently (the user can't register); make it a silent optional skip rather than a warn. FRED_API_KEY and CENSUS_API_KEY are now set on the box. Make sure the FRED and Census refreshes write dated point-in-time rows and that data-audit reports them. Pick a sensible default series set relevant to the AI supply chain (power and electricity, industrial production, semis, construction, rates, inflation, labor). Tests and ruff must pass; export the tarball. No paid replay.

L5790| 
L5790| TOPIC_SERIES is finalized with DGS10 for rates. The replay _MACRO will include a comment on the series set. FRED fetches will drop vintages after the end date. Census data will use a 70-day publication lag.
L5790| 
L5790| Census rows will be filtered by realtime_start against the end date. A 70-day lag window that is too short will return zero dated observations, which the audit will flag. Two-country Census HS rows will have their values summed. FRED fetch will be structured so tests can monkeypatch httpx.get to capture vintage parameters.
L5790| 
L5790| A unit test for the Census HS pipeline will verify country-value summation and 70-day publication lag without any HTTP calls.
L5790| 
L5790| The 70-day publication lag for Census data will be computed with timedelta rather than hardcoded, since the exact date shifts between leap and non-leap years.
L5790| 
L5790| The test will assert the 70-day lag via timedelta. A row is hidden before its publication date and visible on that date. The fetcher returns unavailable for malformed payloads.
L5790| 
L5790| A unit test will mock a Census error response containing the API key and assert that the secret is stripped from the returned status.
L5790| 
L5790| Census HS fetch parameters will be validated: commodity code 8542, level HS4, and a time range containing 2024-01. The IMPCH series is skipped when no API key is configured. The data audit query for industry spans will use a SQL join in the FROM clause.
L5790| 
L5790| The `_span` helper interpolates its WHERE clause directly, so the source filter must be a quoted literal after validating it against `{fred, eia, census}`.
L5790| 
L5790| The audit query will fall back to "fred" if the source is invalid. EIA ingestion is optional, so its failure notes are suppressed and it is excluded from replay macros. Unused imports such as fetch_eia should be removed, and remember_decisions in loop.py needs to be placed after size_position.
L5790| 
L5790| remember_decisions is imported in baselines and called after plan_orders. The rules-only path stamps selected names against existing positions, so the next decision thesis gate works correctly. Equal-weight baseline uses _buy_cash directly and skips cooldowns. The sixty_forty and spy baselines also bypass plan_orders. compute_ratio_block may be slow but only runs for orders that reach that branch. apply_churn mutates order dictionaries in place, which is acceptable.
L5790| 
L5790| The thesis gate correctly blocks buy top-ups when drift is absent. Weekly monitoring notes are appended once per non-rebalance day even if no orders execute, which is intended for daily runs. The audit impact of these notes is being checked.
L5790| 
L5790| The weekly monitoring notes are not uncited facts; they are guard notes and churn notes. The simulation test only checks that equity remains positive and deterministic, so the weekly cooldown will not break it. On Monday the demo fixture capital of 1000 supports eight equal-weight positions at roughly 125 each, which clears the fifty-dollar floor and the fifteen-percent cap.
L5790| 
L5790| Stop-loss and floor rules will be applied inside `orders_toward` alongside churn logic. A shared `_draft_orders` helper is being considered to unify the two order loops, though they currently diverge slightly on cap-reduction detection.
L5790| 
L5790| A `_forced_stops` helper is being added to identify positions that have hit their stop-loss threshold. It calculates each lot’s average cost and flags tickers whose current price falls at or below the configured percentage below that average.
L5790| 
L5790| A `_drawdown_review` helper is being added to flag portfolio drawdowns against the configured derisk threshold. In `plan_orders`, forced stops zero out raw weights before gap and side calculations, and the final trade gate will block orders when the gap is below the floor unless the reason is a hard trigger.
L5790| 
L5790| A `_trade_reason` helper is being added to classify each order as a stop, cap reduction, drawdown, or rebalance. `orders_toward` will compute the `reduced` set by comparing raw weights against outcome weights.
